questions.problem: Carmen, an experienced seamstress, bought $15\,\text{m}$ of drill fabric. The total she paid, expressed as a **decimal number**, was $$${{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
To find out the amount of money that Carmen must pay, we need to multiply $15$ by $3.48.$

We proceed by multiplying the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  &  &  & \,\,\,\,\,\begin{aligned}\boxed{} \\ \boxed{2}\end{aligned}\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned}\boxed{} \\ \boxed{4}\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  &  &  & \,\,\,\,3\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,.4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,7\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,3\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We now count the total number of decimal places in the two factors.

There are $2$ decimal places in $3.48.$ 
Therefore, the product will also have $2$ decimal places.

So, we take our value of $5220$ and add a decimal point to make a number with $2$ decimal places.

$$
52\,\overset{↓}{.}\,\,\,{{20}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ digits}}
$$

Therefore, Carmen must pay $$3.48\times 15=$52.20.$

questions.problem:
Carmen cuts a piece of drill fabric with a length of $2\,\frac{1}{4}\,\text{m}$ to make a tablecloth. If the fabric has a width of $1\,\frac{1}{2}\,\text{m},$ what will be the area of the tablecloth? Express your answer as a **mixed number** in simplest form.

The tablecloth will have an area of
{{field-1}}
${\text{m}}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The tablecloth will have an area of $(2\,\frac{1}{4}\times 1\,\frac{1}{2}){\text{m}}^{2}.$

First, we write $2\,\frac{1}{4}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
2\,\frac{1}{4}=\frac{(2\times 4)+1}{4}=\frac{9}{4}
$$

We also write $1\,\frac{1}{2}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
1\,\frac{1}{2}=\frac{(1\times 2)+1}{2}=\frac{3}{2}
$$

Now, we can multiply the two numbers. We multiply the numerators, and we multiply the denominators:

$$
\frac{9}{4}\times \frac{3}{2}=\frac{9\times 3}{4\times 2}=\frac{27}{8}
$$

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

$$
\frac{27}{8}=3\,\text{R}3=3\,\frac{3}{8}.
$$

questions.problem: Carmen cuts two pieces of drill fabric with lengths of $\frac{5}{6}\,\text{m}$ and $\frac{9}{7}\,\text{m}.$ The sum of the lengths of the two pieces of fabric is{{field-1}}$\text{m}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The sum of the lengths of the two pieces of fabric is $(\frac{5}{6}+\frac{9}{7})\text{m}.$

To add two fractions with unlike denominators, we need to express each fraction as an equivalent fraction with a common denominator.

Let's look at the denominators:

$$
\frac{5}{6}+\frac{9}{7}
$$

The least common denominator of $6$ and $7$ is $42.$

To put $\frac{5}{6}$ over a denominator of $42,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $7:$

$$
\frac{5}{6}=\frac{5\times 7}{6\times 7}=\frac{35}{42}
$$

To put $\frac{9}{7}$ over a denominator of $42,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $6:$

$$
\frac{9}{7}=\frac{9\times 6}{7\times 6}=\frac{54}{42}
$$

We can now add the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we add the numerators.

$$
\frac{35}{42}+\frac{54}{42}=\frac{89}{42}
$$

Expressing this fraction as a mixed number, we get

$$
\frac{89}{42}=2\,\frac{5}{42}.
$$

Therefore, the sum of the lengths of the two pieces of fabric is $2\,\frac{5}{42}\,\text{m}.$

questions.problem:
Carmen has a piece of fabric with a length of $5\,\frac{1}{4}\,\text{m}.$ She accidentally spills coffee on this piece, so she decides to cut out and discard $1\,\frac{1}{5}\,\text{m}$ of fabric. How long is the remaining piece of fabric? Express your answer as a **mixed number** in simplest form.

The remaining piece of fabric has a length of
{{field-1}}
$\text{m}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The new piece of fabric has a length of $(5\,\frac{1}{4}-1\,\frac{1}{5})\text{m}$ long.

To subtract two mixed numbers, we subtract whole numbers from whole numbers and fractions from fractions.

Subtracting the whole numbers, we get $5-1=4.$ 

Now we subtract the fractions:

$$
\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5}
$$

Let's look at the denominators. The least common denominator of $4$ and $5$ is $20.$

To put $\frac{1}{4}$ over a denominator of $20,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $5:$

$$
\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1\times 5}{4\times 5}=\frac{5}{20}
$$

To put $\frac{1}{5}$ over a denominator of $20,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $4:$

$$
\frac{1}{5}=\frac{1\times 4}{5\times 4}=\frac{4}{20}
$$

We can now subtract the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we subtract the numerators:

$$
\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5}=\frac{5}{20}-\frac{4}{20}=\frac{1}{20}
$$

Therefore,

$$
5\,\frac{1}{4}-1\,\frac{1}{5}=4\,\frac{1}{20}.
$$
